_note: Plain-English translations (Q9). Served via /api/glossary; edit this file, no rebuild needed. 'plain' = what it is; 'why' = why you'd care.

expected_range.plain: The band tomorrow's close should land in about 4 days out of 5, based on how much this stock has actually moved over the last 20 sessions.
expected_range.why: It's the only number in this app with hard evidence behind it: this exact construction covered 80.5% of 9,620 historical next-day moves. It says nothing about direction — only size.

daily_sigma.plain: The stock's average-ish daily wiggle, from 20-day realized volatility de-annualized to one day.
daily_sigma.why: Everything range-related is built from this. A '2σ day' means a move twice the typical size.

rv_20d.plain: How much the stock actually moved over the last 20 sessions, annualized. Backward-looking fact, not a forecast.
rv_20d.why: High realized vol = wide expected range. This is measured, not implied by options prices.

move_z.plain: Today's move divided by the typical daily move. 0.5 = quiet day, 2.0 = unusually large day (rarer than ~95% of days).
move_z.why: Answers 'is this drop actually a big deal for THIS stock?' — a 2% day is normal for COIN and wild for KO.

band_coverage.plain: The percent of days in a 2-year, 9,620-row backtest where this exact band construction contained the next day's close. Target: 80%.
band_coverage.why: This is the receipt. If coverage were 60% or 95%, the band would be miscalibrated. It's 77.5–83% across all 20 tested tickers, 80.5% overall.

setup_score.plain: A 0–100 rollup of observable signals (momentum, news, options positioning, analyst shifts, social chatter). 50 = neutral, higher = more bullishly aligned.
setup_score.why: A structured way to see how the usual signals line up. It does NOT predict tomorrow: the same signal families failed direction prediction across ~9,600 backtested calls.

lean.plain: The Setup Score collapsed to a word: BULLISH (≥60), NEUTRAL, or BEARISH (≤40). No confidence percentage on purpose.
lean.why: Direction-confidence numbers were empirically fiction in the parent experiment; the lean is a label, not a probability.

momentum.plain: Where price sits vs its own 20-day and 50-day averages, with extremes damped. Above both = positive; below both = negative.
momentum.why: The classic trend snapshot. Note: at a 1-day horizon this signal predicted nothing in our backtest — it's context, not an edge.

news_sentiment.plain: Finnhub's bullish-vs-bearish split of the past week's news coverage, weighted by how many articles there were.
news_sentiment.why: A 90/10 bullish split on 3 articles is noise; on 40 articles it reflects the actual news tone.

options_positioning.plain: Today's put volume divided by call volume. Below ~0.7: crowd leaning bullish (more calls). Above ~1.1: leaning bearish or hedging.
options_positioning.why: Shows what option traders are paying for today. Session-volume based, so early-morning readings are thin.

implied_move.plain: What the options market charges for an at-the-money straddle at the nearest expiry, as ±% of the stock price — its own version of an expected range.
implied_move.why: Compare with our 80% range: options pricing a much bigger move than realized vol usually means an event (earnings) is in the window.

atm_iv.plain: The volatility the options market is pricing at the money, annualized.
atm_iv.why: IV above realized vol = options expensive vs recent reality (event risk or fear premium); below = cheap.

analyst_trend.plain: How the buy/hold/sell mix shifted vs last month. Shifts matter; the level is mostly already in the price.
analyst_trend.why: Rating CHANGES carry residual information (experiment decision D12). We deliberately don't show price targets — they weren't available from any secured source, and levels are stale anyway.

social_buzz.plain: StockTwits users self-tag posts bullish/bearish. This is that polarity, scaled by how active the stream is.
social_buzz.why: A read on retail mood. Thin streams (a few tagged posts) are heavily discounted.

vol_factor.plain: When current 20-day vol is calmer than its 60-day baseline, signal alignment counts slightly more (×up to 1.15); in turbulence, less (×down to 0.85).
vol_factor.why: Vol regime isn't bullish or bearish — it's how much to trust the other signals. That's why it scales the score instead of adding to it.

pe_ttm.plain: Price divided by the last year of earnings per share. How many dollars you pay per dollar of annual profit.
pe_ttm.why: The bluntest valuation yardstick. Only meaningful vs the company's own history and its sector.

eps_ttm.plain: Profit per share over the last four quarters.
eps_ttm.why: The E in P/E. Growth here is what earnings season is about.

market_cap.plain: Share price × shares outstanding — the market's price for the whole company.
market_cap.why: Sets the size regime: mega-caps move on macro, small caps on their own news.

revenue_growth.plain: Sales over the last 12 months vs the 12 before.
revenue_growth.why: Growth stories live and die on this line staying up and to the right.

gross_margin.plain: What's left of each revenue dollar after direct costs.
gross_margin.why: The ceiling on profitability; erosion here is an early warning.

operating_margin.plain: Profit from actually running the business, per revenue dollar, before interest and taxes.
operating_margin.why: Separates efficient operators from companies buying growth with losses.

net_margin.plain: The bottom line: cents of profit per revenue dollar after everything.
net_margin.why: The number that eventually has to justify the valuation.

dividend_yield.plain: Annual dividends as a % of today's price.
dividend_yield.why: Income context — relevant to your income-sleeve overlap checks.

beta.plain: How much this stock tends to move when the market moves 1%. Beta 1.5 ≈ amplifies the market by half again.
beta.why: Distinguishes 'stock moved because the market moved' from stock-specific action. Computed from 60 days of daily returns.

correlation.plain: How reliably this stock moves WITH the market, from −1 to +1 (60-day daily returns).
correlation.why: High correlation means SPY is most of the story; low means idiosyncratic drivers dominate.

week52_position.plain: Where today's price sits between the 52-week low (0%) and high (100%).
week52_position.why: Instant context for 'is this beaten down or at highs?' before you read anything else.

earnings_countdown.plain: Trading sessions until the next scheduled report.
earnings_countdown.why: THE caveat on the expected range: the band is calibrated for normal days, and earnings days are exactly when ±1.28σ breaks. Treat the band as unreliable inside an earnings window.

earnings_surprise.plain: Last four quarters: reported EPS vs the street's estimate, as a % beat or miss.
earnings_surprise.why: Habitual beaters and missers behave differently into a print; also calibrates how seriously to take estimates.

volume_z.plain: Yesterday's trading volume vs its 20-day average, in standard deviations.
volume_z.why: Abnormal attention. |z| > 2 means something drew a crowd — check the headlines.

sma20_dist.plain: How far price is above (+) or below (−) its 20-day moving average, in %.
sma20_dist.why: Short-term stretch: far above = extended, far below = washed out. Not predictive at 1 day — measured.

sma50_dist.plain: Same as above with a 50-day window — the medium-term trend line most chartists watch.
sma50_dist.why: Crossing it is a widely watched (and widely front-run) signal.

put_call_none.plain: This ticker has no listed options (common for trust ETFs like PHYS/PSLV), or volume is still ~zero this session.
put_call_none.why: Absence of options data is normal for some instruments — the score just reweights around it.

buzz.plain: This week's article count vs the stock's weekly average. 2.0 = twice the usual coverage.
buzz.why: Attention spikes precede volatility more reliably than they precede direction.

stale_data.plain: The source failed on the last refresh, so you're seeing the previous successful fetch, with its age.
stale_data.why: Honest degradation: old-but-labeled beats blank, and beats silently-wrong.

context_hash.plain: A fingerprint of the exact analysis snapshot a Claude discussion was based on.
context_hash.why: If the data has moved a lot since, the discussion is flagged as possibly stale.

ownership.plain: Your actual holding in this ticker, read (read-only) from the Portfolio app's database.
ownership.why: Research with skin-in-the-game context: P&L, cost basis, and portfolio weight beside the analysis.

watchlist_tags.why: Slice the watchlist your way — separate from the Portfolio app's income-focused list.

coverage_target.plain: The band is built to contain the next close 80% of the time — no more, no less.
coverage_target.why: A 100%-coverage band would be uselessly wide. 80% is the deliberate trade: tight enough to mean something, wide enough to be right 4 days in 5.

asset_type.plain: Equity, ETF, or trust — drives which sections apply (ETFs skip fundamentals/analyst sections).
asset_type.why: An ETF with no earnings or analyst coverage isn't 'missing data' — those concepts don't apply.

earnings_move.plain: Two numbers side by side: what the options market charges for the next earnings reaction (implied), and what this stock actually did on its last ~8 earnings days (history).
earnings_move.why: The ratio is the tell: options pricing 2× the stock's own history means the market smells an unusual event; well under 1× means complacency. Neither says WHICH direction.

pead.plain: After a big earnings surprise, prices have historically kept drifting in the surprise's direction for roughly 60 trading days — one of the most-replicated patterns in finance research.
pead.why: Context for the weeks after a report: a big beat that's still drifting is behaving normally. A documented historical tendency — not a guarantee, and it can stop working.

insiders_cluster.plain: Two or more different insiders bought stock on the open market within about two weeks — filtered to real purchases (code P), excluding stock awards, option exercises, and tax sales.
insiders_cluster.why: Research (Cohen–Malloy–Pomorski) shows routine insider trades mean ~nothing, while clustered open-market buys carried real information — on a MULTI-MONTH horizon, not next week.

short_interest.plain: How many shares are currently sold short, per FINRA's official bi-monthly report, shown as a % of shares outstanding (true 'float' data isn't freely available — we label honestly).
short_interest.why: High and rising short interest = a crowded bet against the stock; it can mean informed skepticism, squeeze fuel, or both. The data lags by days-to-weeks by design.

days_to_cover.plain: Short interest divided by average daily volume — how many normal trading days shorts would need to buy their way out.
days_to_cover.why: The squeeze-mechanics number: 5+ days means the exit is narrow if the crowd is ever forced to leave at once.

band_engine.plain: Which volatility estimator builds the 80% range: flat 20-day (default), EWMA (weights recent days more), or conformal (empirical quantile, no distribution assumed).
band_engine.why: Each engine shows its measured backtest coverage in Settings. Flat-20d won the validation — the others are offered because the evidence is displayed, not hidden.

diversification_ratio.plain: The average volatility of your holdings divided by your portfolio's actual volatility. 2.0× means diversification is halving your risk; 1.0× means it's doing nothing.
diversification_ratio.why: The one number that says whether owning 12 things is actually different from owning 3.

premium_lens.plain: For each covered-call or cash-secured-put candidate: what the options market says the breach risk is (its delta) next to what this stock's own 2-year history says (validated to ±6–9.5pp at 1–5 week horizons). Positive edge = you're being paid more than the historical risk costs.
premium_lens.why: This is the variance risk premium made visible per strike — the documented, persistent payment for BEARING risk. It is the opposite of predicting direction: assignment still happens, tails are worse than they look (measured, shown), and earnings windows void the math (flagged).

vrp.plain: The app records the options-implied move each time you analyze a ticker, then checks what actually happened. Ratio above 1 = options systematically overpaid realized moves (favorable climate for sellers); below 1 = underpaid.
vrp.why: Nobody sells this history free — the app builds it by being used. Thin at first, honest about it, more valuable every week.

skew_25d.plain: Implied volatility of a ~25-delta put minus a ~25-delta call. Positive = the crowd pays up for crash protection.
skew_25d.why: A fear gauge per ticker: heavy skew makes put-selling richer (you're selling insurance at panic prices) and signals what the market worries about.

rebalance_sandbox.plain: Type hypothetical trades (−$3,000 MSFT, +$2,000 JEPQ) and see the WHOLE portfolio's before/after: tomorrow's dollar range, volatility, diversification, beta, projected income, cash. Nothing executes.
rebalance_sandbox.why: Brokers show the order ticket; nothing shows what a trade does to your book's risk and income before you make it.

research_stance.plain: Claude's reasoned buy/sell/hold/trim/watch call from your latest discussion session — with a horizon and one-line justification, dated, and marked stale when the data has moved since.
research_stance.why: The app itself never computes buy/sell/hold: its signals demonstrably can't call direction (~9,600 backtested predictions). A stance from a full research session — valuation, thesis, risk, news — is a different kind of judgment, and it ages in plain sight instead of pretending to be current.

score_history.plain: The Setup Score recorded each time you analyzed this ticker. Grows as you use the tool.
score_history.why: There's no 30-day backfill because point-in-time sentiment/options history doesn't exist — a reconstructed 'history' would be fiction. This one is real.
